item.title: New EU fishing quotas described as disaster for Irish fishermen
item.description: New EU fishing quotas which will hit Irish fishermen are being described as "a disaster for the fishing industry." Over 2,300 jobs are at risk from the decision made by member states on Saturday to block an arrangement that protects the country's fishing industry. The Killibegs Fishermen's Organisation says the Irish fishing sector will lose around 57 thousand tonnes of fish, which is a hit of around 100 million euro. item.title: Cavan player wins €17 million EuroMillions jackpot
item.description: The National Lottery has confirmed that a lucky Cavan player has won the €17 million jackpot in Friday night’s Euromillions draw. The winning ticket was purchased in a retail store in Cavan, with the exact location to be announced on Tuesday. This is the second Irish EuroMillions jackpot win of 2025, and Cavan’s second millionaire in just two weeks, following a Daily Million top prize on 30th November. item.title: Appeal issued following fatal Monaghan Town collision
item.description: Gardaí are appealing for witnesses following a fatal road traffic collision at Old Cross Square in Monaghan Town. Shortly after 10:15am yesterday morning, Gardaí and emergency services were alerted to the collision, involving a lorry and a pedestrian. The male pedestrian, aged in his 60s died at the scene. item.title: Ireland claim European Cross Country men's team silver
item.description: Ireland claimed a first men’s senior European cross country silver medal in over 20-years taking team silver in Lagoa, Portugal. It was a dramatic day as Ireland claimed a total of four medals. Nick Griggs won U23 gold and led the team to gold. Whereas, 16-year-old Emma Hickey took U20 bronze. Mullingar’s Jack O’Leary led the Irish charge with an excellent fifth place finish in the senior race. While Brian Fay (Raheny Shamrock) took 10th place.
